description_good_justification: README.md and the DESCRIPTION Description field explain what seor does: a metapackage that installs and attaches the seor SEO and web-developer packages with one library() call. Both are rendered at https://seor-272402.gitlab.io.
interact_justification: The homepage https://seor-272402.gitlab.io links to the source repository (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor) and, through DESCRIPTION's BugReports field, to the issue tracker. CONTRIBUTING.md describes how to send merge requests.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains how to report issues and send merge requests on GitLab.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) states the requirements: tests for new code, one NEWS.md bullet per user-facing change, and a passing verification command (lintr plus R CMD check --as-cran, failing on warnings).
floss_license_justification: The package is released under the MIT license.
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license.
license_location_justification: The license is in the repository root: LICENSE (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/LICENSE, the CRAN two-field stub) and LICENSE.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/LICENSE.md, the full MIT text).
documentation_basics_justification: The pkgdown site https://seor-272402.gitlab.io carries the README (installation and use) and an introduction vignette.
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function has roxygen-generated reference documentation, published at https://seor-272402.gitlab.io/reference/.
sites_https_justification: The homepage (https://seor-272402.gitlab.io), the repository (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor) and the download channels use HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: Discussion happens on GitLab issues and merge requests (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/work_items), which are public, searchable and addressable by URL, and need no proprietary client software.
english_justification: DESCRIPTION declares Language: en-US, and all documentation, issues and commit messages are in English.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained; SECURITY-INSIGHTS.yml records repository.status: active.
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public git repository on GitLab: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor. The GitHub repository is a read-only mirror.
repo_track_justification: The repository is git, which records every change, its author and its time.
repo_interim_justification: Work between releases lands on the public main branch through merge requests, not only at release time.
repo_distributed_justification: The repository is git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version number in the DESCRIPTION Version field, following R package conventions.
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/NEWS.md) is the human-readable changelog. Every user-facing change adds a bullet there, and the news-version CI job checks that its top heading matches DESCRIPTION's Version.
report_process_justification: Bug reports go to the GitLab issue tracker (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/work_items), named in CONTRIBUTING.md and in DESCRIPTION's BugReports field.
report_tracker_justification: The project uses GitLab work items as its public issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/work_items.
report_archive_justification: GitLab keeps reports and responses publicly archived and searchable at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/work_items.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md) explains how to report vulnerabilities.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md) sends private reports to a confidential GitLab issue or to the maintainer's email address.
build_justification: The package builds with the standard R CMD build and R CMD INSTALL toolchain.
build_common_tools_justification: The package uses the standard R package toolchain.
build_floss_tools_justification: R and its package toolchain are free and open source software.
test_justification: The package includes an automated testthat suite under tests/testthat, with Cucumber-style behavior specs.
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with testthat::test_local() or devtools::test(), and as part of R CMD check.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for new code.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The GitLab CI pipeline (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/pipelines) runs the full verification chain on every push to main. The same chain runs as a pre-push hook on every branch before it leaves a contributor's machine.
warnings_justification: lintr and R CMD check --as-cran run in the verification chain, locally and in the GitLab pipeline.
warnings_fixed_justification: The verification chain fails on any lint finding or R CMD check warning, so warnings are fixed before merge.
warnings_strict_justification: The verification chain fails on any lint finding or R CMD check warning.
static_analysis_justification: lintr, the common R static analysis tool, runs on every change in the verification chain.
delivery_mitm_justification: seor is installed from GitLab or r-universe (and from CRAN once released), all over HTTPS only.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Installation fetches packages from GitLab, r-universe or CRAN over HTTPS. No hash is retrieved over plain HTTP.
crypto_published_justification: seor implements no cryptography. It only installs and attaches its member packages.
crypto_random_justification: seor generates no cryptographic keys or nonces.
version_semver_justification: DESCRIPTION's Version uses R's x.y.z scheme, with a fourth .9000 component marking development versions (currently 0.0.0.9000).
version_tags_justification: No release exists yet. The release process tags every CRAN version in git and publishes a matching GitLab Release (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/releases), as SECURITY-INSIGHTS.yml records.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed to date. NEWS.md records every user-facing change: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_responses_justification: No bug reports have been filed yet. The maintainer monitors the tracker and responds to reports there: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been filed yet. The maintainer monitors the tracker and responds to requests there: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/work_items
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a report within 7 days: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
test_most_justification: Line coverage measured by covr in the GitLab coverage job is 100% (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/pipelines).
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality ships with tests. For example, adding raddr as a member extended tests/testthat/test-attach.R, and coverage stays at 100%.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states that new code needs tests: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles. seor exposes a minimal surface: it only attaches its member packages and reports name conflicts, takes no untrusted input, and makes no network connections.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common error classes for R packages (unsafe evaluation of input, unvalidated input, dependency risk). seor avoids them by doing nothing beyond attaching packages and reporting conflicts.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known vulnerabilities, and none are outstanding. Reports go through SECURITY.md; the tracker is https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor/-/work_items
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known critical vulnerabilities.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed. A gitleaks scan of the full git history (54 commits, 2026-09-26) found no leaks.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: lintr and R CMD check find defects but are not vulnerability scanners. The osv-audit job checks dependencies against OSV, but it is SCA, not static analysis of seor's code, and it only runs when started by hand.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The verification chain fails on any lintr finding, so static-analysis findings are fixed before merge.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every push: the verification chain is a pre-push hook, and it runs again in the GitLab pipeline on every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (fuzzer, sanitizer or valgrind) is run. seor is pure R with no compiled code.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: seor is pure R with no compiled code, so it contains no memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The testthat suite's expectations are assertions checked at runtime on every run of the verification chain.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run (see dynamic_analysis), so there are no findings to fix.
homepage_url_justification: The project homepage is https://seor-272402.gitlab.io. It is named first in DESCRIPTION's URL field, alongside the GitLab repository https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/seor.
crypto_used_network_justification: seor makes no network connections of its own. Installation is handled by pak or install.packages().
crypto_tls12_justification: seor makes no network connections of its own.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: seor makes no network connections of its own.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: seor makes no network connections of its own.
hardening_justification: Hardening mechanisms such as HTTP security headers apply to web applications. seor is an R library.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitLab, GitLab Pages, r-universe) manage their own authentication. seor runs no site with user passwords.
